children: President Donald Trump is expected to unveil plans Wednesday for roughly $200 billion in South Korean investments in the United States, including about $54 billion tied to the long-delayed Alaska LNG project, Bloomberg News reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the discussions.

The projects would represent the first major commitments under a U.S.-South Korea trade agreement reached last year. Seoul pledged $350 billion in U.S. investments as part of the deal, which lowered U.S. tariffs on South Korean goods to 15%. Of that amount, $150 billion was earmarked for shipbuilding and $200 billion for investments in other strategic industries.

For investors, the announcement could provide new details on several large U.S. energy and infrastructure projects that have been under consideration for the Korean investment fund. Those include a gas-fired power project in Texas, nuclear energy investments and the Alaska LNG development.

The Alaska project would transport natural gas from Alaska's North Slope through a roughly 800-mile pipeline to a liquefaction and export terminal in Nikiski, where LNG could be shipped to Asian markets. The project has been discussed for years but has struggled to secure sufficient commercial commitments and financing. South Korean officials previously expressed caution about its economics.

South Korea has also selected a planned 6.3-gigawatt natural gas power complex in Encinal, Texas, as an initial project under the investment program. The development has been estimated at roughly $22 billion and is intended to help meet rising electricity demand from data centers and semiconductor manufacturing.

Other proposals under discussion have included construction of eight nuclear reactors in the United States and a possible South Korean investment in Westinghouse Electric. The nuclear and Alaska projects had not been finalized as of last week.

Trump is expected to discuss the investment package at the White House on Wednesday. The announcement would mark a significant step toward implementing an agreement that had faced delays as Washington and Seoul negotiated project selection, financing terms and commercial viability.

title: Trump set to unveil $200B South Korean U.S. investment plan
